newsitem.title: USA: American Home unit denies allegations.
newsitem.headline: American Home unit denies allegations.

text.p: Wyeth-Ayerst Laboratories, a subsidiary of American Home Products Corp, on Thursday denied allegations that it failed to provide appropriate warnings on the use of its prescription diet drugs.
On Wednesday, Wyeth-Ayerst, along with several other pharmaceutical companies, was named in a class-action lawsuit filed in federal court in San Francisco.
The suit was filed on behalf of people who had used three popular weight-loss drugs, including Pondimin and Redux, marketed by Wyeth-Ayerst.
The company said it had neither been served with nor seen the lawsuit and could not comment on the details of the suit's allegations.
However, the company said in a statment that it rejected "the allegations mentioned in press reports, that it failed to provide appropriate warnings on the use of these products.
"The Food and Drug Administration has approved the sale of each of these drugs and has at all times approved the warnings provided by Wyeth-Ayerst," the company said.
